items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The two largest farms were owned by the Fergusons and the Hagens.

ctx.x: I also remember that my grand-mother Coleman lived in a 4-room log cabin. Any house built of logs was a cabin and this was the only one in Centerville. I never knew if it was Uncle John that built it.

All around Centerville were farms, and some of them belonging to one family which would run as far as the eye could see. The two largest farms were owned by the Fergusons and the Hagens. The Fergusons' land was on the Lexington and Georgetown Road and the Hagen's farm was on the Lexington Road which ran through Centerville. I loved ponies, and there were thousands of them on these two farms.

Uncle John was a paperhanger. He also put electricity in his house with some system that he bought from Sears and Roebucks mail order house in Chicago. He was the only person to have electricity in the village. He was also the professor of the school, which had studies from the 1st to the 8th grade, all in one room. He was a hard man on children and anyone else who crossed him.
